'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***Several [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[cruise missile]]s strike [[Kyiv]], killing one civilian and injuring four others, according to [[Prosecutor General of Ukraine|Ukraine's Prosecutor General]]. Some of the missiles were launched from [[Tupolev Tu-95]] strategic bombers over the [[Caspian Sea]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-61943252 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/6/26/russia-ukraine-live-news-indonesia-leader-to-visit-kyiv-moscow (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3515432-one-civilian-killed-four-injured-in-russias-missile-attack-on-kyiv.html (Ukrinform)]
***A missile strike kills a civilian and destroys a strategic bridge connecting [[western Ukraine]] with eastern [[battlefield]]s in [[Cherkasy Oblast]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/missile-strikes-kill-one-near-central-ukrainian-city-cherkasy-governor-2022-06-26/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in the Sahel]]
**Two police officers are killed and another is injured in [[Dassari, Benin|Dassari]], [[Benin]], by [[militant]]s suspected to be from [[Niger]] or [[Burkina Faso]]. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/two-police-officers-killed-in-north-benin-attack/47704812 (SwissInfo)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**A [[shootout]] occurs between the [[Mexican federal police]] and [[drug cartel]]s in [[Nuevo León]], close to the [[Mexico–United States border]]. Six officers are killed and four others injured. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/six-police-die-shootout-northern-mexico-2022-06-26/ (Reuters)]
*Two soldiers and seven [[militant]]s are killed in a shootout in [[Ghulam Khan]], [[North Waziristan]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/afghanistan-pakistan-islamabad-taliban-militant-groups-5a10812ec08bf1d5e16fe0c6ea178c26 (AP)]
*Seven [[Sudanese soldier]]s and a civilian are [[summarily executed]] after being held captive in [[Addis Ababa]], [[Ethiopia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/sudan-accuses-ethiopia-executing-7-sudanese-soldiers-civilian-2022-06-26/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 East London tavern disaster]]
**Twenty-one people are found dead at a tavern in [[East London, Eastern Cape]], [[South Africa]]. The cause of their deaths is unclear. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-61941170 (BBC News)]
*One person is killed and another is reported missing after a fire on an inter-island ferry in [[Manila]], [[Philippines]]. [https://apnews.com/article/fires-accidents-philippines-manila-16313cf2b8aa576ef9274a91ebe3c60c (AP)] 
*Two people are killed and nine others are injured in a fire at a market in [[Bangkok]], [[Thailand]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/bangkoks-market-fire-kills-least-2-2022-06-26/ (Reuters)]
*Four people are killed and 322 are injured when a stand in a [[bullring]] collapses in [[El Espinal, Tolima|El Espinal]], [[Colombia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/politics-sports-colombia-caribbean-gustavo-petro-dbba6a7d5b87668ef96c5c14c8e8707a (AP)]
*Three people are killed in [[Brentwood, California|Brentwood]], [[California]], [[United States|U.S.]], when their car collides with an [[Amtrak]] train. [https://www.cbsnews.com/sanfrancisco/news/brentwood-crash-involving-amtrak-train/ (CBS News)]
*Two people are killed and more are missing after heavy flooding in [[Krasnodar region]] and annexed [[Crimea]], [[Russia]]. [https://floodlist.com/europe/russia-floods-sochi-june-2022 (FloodList)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/heavy-rainfall-causes-flooding-russia-annexed-crimea-2022-06-27/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Russia]]
**[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] embarks on [[List of international presidential trips made by Vladimir Putin|a foreign trip]] to [[Tajikistan]] and [[Turkmenistan]], his first since the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russias-putin-make-first-foreign-trip-since-launching-ukraine-war-2022-06-26/ (Reuters)]
*[[48th G7 summit]]
**The [[Group of Seven|G7]] summit kicks off in [[Schloss Elmau]], [[Krün]], [[Bavarian Alps]], [[Germany]], and will last until June 28. [[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Fumio Kishida]] and [[Chancellor of Germany|German Chancellor]] [[Olaf Scholz]] makes their first appearance at the summit. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/white-house/biden-kicks-g7-summit-focus-ukraine-global-economy-rcna35345 (NBC News)] [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2022/06/26/world/fumio-kishida-g7-russia-ukraine/ (''Japan Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[LGBT rights in Turkey]]
**[[Riot]] [[Turkish police|police]] disperse hundreds of people in [[Istanbul]] after the [[government of Turkey|government]] banned the Pride Parade, alleging that the parade could cause "public unrest due to society's sensitivities". [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkish-police-prevent-istanbul-pride-going-ahead-2022-06-26/ (Reuters)]
*[[Nigeria]]'s [[Zamfara State]] begins issuing [[firearms license]]s to citizens so that they can defend themselves from [[Nigerian bandit conflict|bandit gangs]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/nigerian-state-allow-individuals-carry-guns-against-bandits-2022-06-26/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Knesset]] advances a bill, for a possible vote on Wednesday, which would ban indicted politicians from becoming [[Prime Minister of Israel]]. If passed, it would prevent [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] from returning to that post. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/government-advances-problematic-bill-that-would-block-defendant-netanyahus-return/ (''Times of Israel'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021–22 NHL season]]
**In [[ice hockey]], the [[Colorado Avalanche]] [[2022 Stanley Cup Finals|defeat]] the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] in six games to win their first [[Stanley Cup]] since [[2000–01 Colorado Avalanche season|the 2001 season]], thereby dethroning the Lightning in their quest to [[three-peat]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/06/26/sports/colorado-avalanche-tampa-bay-lightning-game-6-stanley-cup.html (''The New York Times'')]
